crawl: Chrome live crawl, same-origin fetch, cache: no-store, sequential per URL, ~07:35-07:55 Vietnam time on 2026-09-30 (one-day step from 29 Sep)
method: TTFB measured with performance.now() around a sequential fetch of each URL with a 15 s abort. Words counted on a body clone with script/style/noscript/template removed. Schema blocks counted as application/ld+json elements, @type walked through @graph. Internal links are unique same-origin paths per page.
score_rationale: Health HOLDS at 95 (raw 95.40 -> 95.15). Exactly one sub-score moved. PERFORMANCE 99 -> 98: the TTFB ceiling rose 581 -> 650 ms and the site mean 323 -> 342 ms, with the slowest page now /articles/3d-renders-for-builders-melbourne at 650 ms. This is drift inside a healthy band rather than a regression - all 118 pages still answered in under a second, nothing landed in the 1-3 s band and nothing exceeded 3 s - but 650 ms is above the 617 ms ceiling that scored 98 two days ago, so the point earned yesterday is given back. CRAWLABILITY HOLDS at 98: the /articles overlay was re-checked today and is still gone (zero elements at z-index >= 9999, zero fixed elements covering 95 pct or more of the viewport, elementFromPoint at the viewport centre resolving to ordinary content, 109 article links clickable), and there are still zero orphans with every page carrying at least two inbound links. It stays short of 100 for the same single reason as yesterday: the site-wide promoted link the template dropped on 28 Sep has NOT returned - total distinct internal links are 2,711 for a second consecutive crawl against 2,802 before the regression. STRUCTURED DATA HOLDS at 92 - 116 of 118 pages carry schema, 394 blocks, FAQPage on 82 of 95 articles (86.3 pct) for a fourth crawl with the same 13 articles missing it. ONPAGE HOLDS at 92 - byte-identical on every signal, still 118 images without alt text. CONTENT HOLDS at 93 - the word total is 241,329 for a second crawl, exactly unchanged, with no new article since 24 Sep and no article expanded this cycle.

pages.note: 117 sitemap HTML pages plus /login. All 118 returned 200. No new page and no removed page against 29 Sep; the page set is identical for a twentieth crawl.

sitemap.linked_absent_method: Re-measured this run from the inbound-link graph over all 118 crawled pages, counting only same-origin HTML paths.
sitemap.legacy_recheck_note: All ten legacy long-slug article URLs were re-fetched from the origin today: ten of ten returned 200 and ten of ten are self-canonical. No regression for another day.

ttfb_ms.note: THE CEILING ROSE 581 -> 650 ms and the slowest page is an article again: /articles/3d-renders-for-builders-melbourne at 650 ms, ahead of /articles/3d-virtual-tour-off-the-plan-apartments at 604 ms. Core rose 336 -> 381 ms, articles 325 -> 340 ms and projects 255 -> 264 ms, so every group drifted the same way. Site mean 323 -> 342 ms and median 270 -> 276 ms. The homepage came in at 515 ms, no longer the fastest of the core pages but well inside the band. ALL 118 PAGES STILL ANSWERED UNDER ONE SECOND, with zero in the 1-3 s band and zero over 3 s.

content.note: THE WORD TOTAL IS EXACTLY UNCHANGED at 241,329 - not a single page gained or lost a word this cycle, against +1,752 words across five articles yesterday. No new article since 24 Sep, a sixth consecutive day. The thirteen pages under 300 words are the same thirteen: the six project pages (170-188 words each) plus /projects, /contact, /modules, /interiors, /model, /start-interactive and /login. The six project pages remain the clearest content gap on the site.

schema.note: Byte-identical to 29 Sep: 116 of 118 pages carry schema (394 JSON-LD blocks), the two without are /login and /start-interactive, and FAQPage coverage is frozen at 82 of 95 articles (86.3 pct) for a FOURTH consecutive crawl with the same 13 articles missing it. Article and BlogPosting appear on all 95 articles and BreadcrumbList on 114 pages.

heading_skips.note: No heading level is skipped anywhere on the site.

onpage.note: Byte-identical to 29 Sep on every on-page signal: 118/118 for exactly one h1, title, meta description, canonical and self-canonical; zero heading-level skips; meta descriptions run 83-189 characters, all inside the useful range. The alt-text gap is unchanged at 118 of 1,387 images (1,269 with alt, 91.5 pct) and is confirmed again this crawl to be EXACTLY ONE image per page - a single template fix closes all 118 at once.

crawlability.note: THE OVERLAY FIX HELD FOR A SECOND DAY. A live load of /articles, waited out 15 seconds, returns zero elements at z-index >= 9999 anywhere in the document, zero fixed elements covering 95 pct or more of the viewport, and elementFromPoint at the viewport centre resolves to an ordinary static content div rather than a blocking overlay. 109 article links are directly clickable in the DOM and the hub HTML is byte-identical at 279,515 bytes. Confirmed resolved, not merely absent once. ZERO ORPHANS for a nineteenth day and zero articles that depend on the hub alone - every page carries at least two inbound internal links (minimum 2, maximum 117 on the homepage). THE ONE OUTSTANDING ITEM IS UNCHANGED: total distinct internal links are 2,711 for a second consecutive crawl, still short of the 2,802 before the 28 Sep template regression, so the site-wide promoted link has not come back.

tag_check.note: Homepage DOM tag check: window.google_tag_manager exposes 17 keys including the GTM container GTM-PZ9N8QTR, the Google Ads tag AW-18039433307 and the GA4 tag G-43HE633LGK. dataLayer length 3. window.gtag is undefined, as it has been on every previous check - GTM loads the tags itself. Identical to 29 Sep.

roadmap: P0 - restore the site-wide promoted link the article template dropped on 28 Sep. Total distinct internal links have now sat at 2,711 for two consecutive crawls against 2,802 before the regression; the featured block promotes three articles where it used to promote four. This is the only thing still holding crawlability below 100.
P1 - batch a FAQPage block into the 13 articles still missing one; coverage has been frozen at 82 of 95 (86.3 pct) for FOUR crawls and the method is proven on the other 82.
P1 - add alt text to the single template image repeated on every page. One template fix closes all 118 missing alts at once and is the only thing capping the onpage sub-score.
P2 - lift the six project pages off roughly 178 words each. They are the thinnest real content on the site and the clearest remaining content gap.

P3 - watch the TTFB ceiling. It moved 581 -> 650 ms this crawl and every group drifted the same way; nothing is slow yet (all 118 pages under 1 s) but a second consecutive rise would be worth investigating at the host.
P3 - publish. No new article since 24 Sep, six days, and the word total did not move at all this cycle.
process_note: One crawl served both this audit and the SEO report in the same run, so TTFB, word counts, schema counts and the internal-link graph agree between the two reports by construction.
